newsitem.title: USA: S&P says challenges abound for UK cable companies.
newsitem.headline: S&P says challenges abound for UK cable companies.

text.p: U.K. cable companies are being confronted by a variety of challenges, but their financial situation should improve over the long-term, Standard & Poor's said.
S&P made its comments in an article in the most recent issue of CreditWeek, a weekly magazine published by the rating agency.

S&P recently lowered the ratings on four U.K. cable companies, citing their strained financial profile amid weakened industry fundamentals. It pointed out that cable operators are experiencing lower and slower growth in cash flow generation than was originally anticipated.

The U.S. rating agency said U.K. cable companies are facing numerous challenges including mixed consumer acceptance of their cable and telephone services and formidable competition from companies such as digital satellite television provider BSkyB.
U.K. cable companies are also hampered by their high and growing debt burdens which are required to fund their operating losses and complete their network buildouts, it said.
But S&P pointed out that a favorable regulatory environment, particularly in the telecommunications area, is mitigating some of these risks.

The 1990 deregulation of the U.K. telecommunications duopoly allowed cable operators to carve out a significant niche in the telecommunications sector, S&P said. Other regulations limiting the flexibilty of British Telecommunications PLC's local loop pricing have also benefitted these companies.
S&P noted, "The U.K. cable industry increasingly is becoming a telecoms industry, with a large portion of revenues coming from non-cable (mainly telephone) sources."
S&P added U.K. cable companies that offer digital services have the opportunity to benefit from an increasingly diverse revenue source.

Two U.K. cable providers, Cable and Wireless Communications Plc (CWC) and Telewest Communications Plc, plan to offer digital services that will greatly increase the number of channels and services the companies will offer.

Looking out to the future, S&P said it expected industry consolidation, such as the recent merger of Bell Cablemedia, Videotron and NYNEX Cablecomms into CWC to continue. It said consolidation may help the industry reduce its costs and increase its leverage with programming suppliers such as BSkyB.

S&P concluded, "If cable operators are able to secure a position in the television market and establish alternative programming sources while creating a competitive national telephone network, their business profiles and overall credit quality should improve accordingly over the longer term."
